text: There's something off with those researchers.
The people who come back from that lab smell funny.
I hear screams at night sometimes.
I heard Crustacean Corporation is experimenting on those poor people!
You should vote for fish rights even if you're not a fish.
Hey at least all of the predators are doing this voluntarily. And they're getting paid for it!
Do you think any research positions are still open?
Crustacean corp offered me a job, but there’s something not right about those guys
I’m volunteering for the new research project!

nodesVet: Hasn't gotten better? We'll run some tests and get back to you.
He's a little sick. Give him this medication every day.
Tests came back positive, I recommend immediate treatment.
I'm so sorry but he didn't pull through.
ittyBitty: My best friend’s name is Samuel! What’s your best friend’s name?
Mom always looks so cool in her white jacket!
Mom makes the best food in the whole wide sea!
School’s so boring…mister will you play with me and Samuel? …Aww ok.
What candies do I like? Mm, I like jawbreakers and rock candies, but lollipops are my fav!
Mister! I got my favorite strawberry-banana lollipop today! Do you want one too?
They didn’t have strawberry-banana at the store today…That’s my favorite…
I like my mom, I like Samuel, I like strawberry-banana lollipops…and I like you too!
protestorCatfish: I just love the rain, don’t you?
I don’t need to buy a ticket for a plant, right?
I can bring my sign on the train, right?
My plant Shelldon looks a little wilted today
I put all my pots outside today to catch the water
Can I bring eggplant parm on the train?
You should come to my next protest!
You ever think the dark clouds are trying to tell us something?
The new labs are just further marginalizing us fish
If I chain myself to the front of the lab, do you think they’d cease operations?
horseshoeCrab: Ah, this aged shell of mine creaks so. Send an old soul on his way, young lad?
There was a time when all beings roamed the seabed. Indeed, one misses those days long gone.
Those who one once traveled with are now long gone, their traces vanished from this world.
Hmph! Compared to yesteryear, the hunters of this age are scrawny beings.
Forgive this body’s torpidness; one has been bound to this wheelchair for a long while.
Young lad, don’t make the same mistakes one did. If you can save someone, do not stand by and send them to their deaths.
One still hears their voices screaming…one cannot tell if they are from dreams of old or sufferings of the present.
Technology and transportation are so advanced these days…one cannot help but feel like a foreigner in this age.
Young lad, you should get out and enjoy this life with your loved ones. Do not dedicate your life to survival, and end up being the last lonely one.
...My friends? …They were known in the history books as brave warriors, but one wishes to remember them outside of their assigned descriptions.
isobelle: I need more money to afford all my bows
I wish it were a bit colder today
You’d look cuter with a bow too!
I can’t wait to curl up on the train and read
You aren’t supposed to wear blue today, you know
Do you think I talk too quietly?
I don’t like making eye contact. Could you not look at me when I look at you?
I hope that new lab could use a secretary... I’ve been applying since forever
seaStarDad: Hey kiddo! I’m fresh out of jokes, if you’ve got any, let minnow!
I hope Billie and Millie are doing well in school… nah, they’re stars like you and me kiddo!
Psst hey, know where the best flower field around here is? No this isn’t a lead-up to a punchline, I’m being serious!
I’m so pumped right now! Managed to snag the last few Basalt concert tickets before I got off work!
Ooh, you look real fresh today! Got a date? Need some tips? Don’t worry, they’re free of charge! Unlike these ticket prices…
This wildflower bouquet? I make one for my wife every time I get to go back home.
Hey what did the two oceans say to each other? Nothing, they just waved! HAHA! …oh, I guess you’ve heard that one too much, hmm…
I just want my family to be safe and live happily.
I think I’m going to quit real soon. I just…I can find a safer job out there, closer to my family.
granny: Gramps told me you were handsome and he was right!
Any crustaceans you’ve got your eye on?
Today is a beautiful day isn’t it?
I just love taking the train this time of year
It was me and Gramps' 50th anniversary yesterday!
Let me set you up with my granddaughter... You’d love her!
I found a husband for that granddaughter I mentioned and they're so happy
I heard you might have a secret admirer
I see the way the mailkeeper looks at you, he’s smitten
If you happen to have a date with that mailkeeper in the future, I’d wear something else
gramps: I hope they give you enough breaks here
Make sure to stop and smell the sea breeze
How many times can you let the same thing get you down?
Remember to tell others that you love them
Never forget you can always begin anew
Sunny days and rainy days are both days where anything is possible
Don’t wait for new opportunities go find them
In bad times, good things are always waiting just over the horizon
Taking care of something else gives you reason to keep going
gramps_ending: You doing alright, kid?
Something on your mind?
A lot of folks out there owe you their livelihoods, you know.
A lot of lives might have been ruined, if it weren’t for you.
But that’s cold comfort, ain’t it?
I’m sorry about your pet, kid.
I started noticing a while back you took it out less and less, and lately I haven’t seen it at all.
Something tells me you had to give it up.
Can I tell you a story?
Back when I was young I met a girl. Loved her with all my heart.
We rushed through things, got married, and I ended up with a family before I could really handle it.
We had trouble making ends meet, even with both of us working jobs.
One of us needed to get an education if we wanted to give our kids the lives they deserved.
So I joined the navy. It paid well and it made sure I could get through college by the end of things.
I spent two years there, during the Ammonite War, just loading craft. Arming them with torpedoes.
I never even set foot on a ship.
Well, the war ended, I got a degree in engineering, and started working for a train company.
A little one, a subsidiary of a place called "Crustacean Corporation."
They were doing some sketchy things, but I didn’t think much of it. The job was paying for my own kids to go to college, after all.
It let me afford a trip around the world each year.
Then one year, I took a trip to Ammonatia.
I stumbled on one of the places the navy visited, and saw fossil after fossil after fossil littering the ground…
…all surrounded by old torpedo shells.
And I realized, like you did, that I was responsible.
I never captained the ships.
I never fired the torpedoes.
But any one of the torpedoes there could have been loaded by me.
And maybe if I hadn’t been there, a few more ammonites would have lived.
I quit my job as a train engineer the moment I got back.
I started working at a mom and pop mechanic’s shop instead.
I didn’t go on another vacation for thirty years.
But I can sleep well each night, knowing I left that train company before…
…this happened.
It’s gonna be a hard few weeks, kid. And a hard few years after that, while you get back on your feet.
But I hope you don’t regret a second of it.
vet1: Hey there, how are we doing today?
Just here for a regular checkup for your lil’ one here? Mm, we’ll see about that…
Ohhhh…hmm…
Well, your buddy here is not doing too hot right now!
Look at him! One of his legs is shorter than the other; this is clearly a sign of malnutrition!
No no, I’m not saying you’re not doing a good job of raising them.
Your isopod simply isn’t getting enough nutrients.
You know how the store brands are nowadays, always processed and full of fillers.
Here, I personally recommend this brand right here.
It’s a bit more expensive, yes, but I promise it is much more nutrient-packed and natural.
I highly suggest you switch soon, otherwise your isopod will be at considerable risk of falling ill.
What do I mean? You see…it’s not just the food.
It appears your isopod has a severe chronic respiratory illness.
This appears to be something genetic; your isopod’s gills are unable to properly absorb oxygen.
Over time, this will cause severe issues and will certainly lead to an early death.
We’ll need to take a tissue sample for testing to see which medicine will work best.
At the very worst, we may need to do surgery to replace your isopod’s gills with artificial ones.
I’m very sorry to be the bearer of such bad news.
I’ll prescribe some medicinal flakes for this week, and we’ll get that sample taken today.
Please trust that I will do my absolute best to save your beloved isopod.
Your total today comes up to about 800 dollars.
vet2: Hey there, hope you’re both doing well!
I’ll first do a wellness checkup on your lil’ guy, and then we’ll discuss the test results.
Well, here’s the good news. Your isopod is relatively stable and doing much better than last week.
The bad news is the test results.
From now on, your isopod will need regular booster shots and medication.
However, this won’t be enough. The best solution is artificial gills.
Unfortunately, the level of damage is too severe. Shots and medication are only temporary measures.

Do you think you’ll ever love someone more than your isopod?

You spend money on things besides your isopod, right…?
We should get lunch sometime when we’re both on break, I promise I won’t bore you…
You ever think about getting out of here..? I do, but you make staying worthwhile.
You know, I’ve started to wonder if I see you less than your vet does…

mailkeeperGoodEnding: I knew you were more than just a pretty face, you’ve got strong morals too. I like that in a person.
A lot of people want to thank you, you know
